notes: Event date: USHMM and Wikipedia: the 4th Armored Division landed at Utah Beach on 11 July 1944. Event definition: the first landing of the division at Utah Beach. The 13 July row (preferred) is the CMH ETO-OB chronology date for arrival on the Continent, with the division command post at Mesnil-St-Martin on that date; the two may describe different phases (first elements ashore, main body ashore, command post established) rather than a disagreement. A reviewer said the 704th Tank Destroyer Battalion boarded 11 July and landed 12 July; that was not confirmed (tankdestroyer.net, citing Yeide, has the battalion landing on 13 July). Location: Utah Beach area (OpenStreetMap Nominatim); the Mesnil-St-Martin command post this row reused belongs to the 13 July row only.

location_name: vicinity of Mesnil-St-Martin, Manche (unresolved CMH place name)
notes: Event date: CMH ETO-OB chronology: arrived on the Continent 13 July 1944. Event definition: arrival of the division on the Continent as CMH records it, with the command post at the vicinity of Mesnil-St-Martin, Manche, listed on this date (CMH gives the CP only as a vicinity of the town). Wikipedia and USHMM give 11 July for the Utah Beach landing (alternate row): the rows may describe different phases of the landing. Location caveat: the CMH CP name "Mesnil-St-Martin" could not be resolved to a Manche commune with certainty. The Nominatim match used before (about 49.0, -1.29, near Percy) lies roughly 50 km from the landing beaches and is inconsistent with the later CP at Méautis (17-18 July) and with a unit that had just landed at Utah Beach (Coutances was not taken until 28 July); the point is therefore unreliable and is kept only as a very wide inferred point. The unit was in the Cotentin beachhead assembly area (a 37th Tank Battalion report puts the division assembly area in use on 12 July).
